topic: Water-cement ratio and its effect on strength, workability and durability of concrete
source: 601-80.json, 681-760.json, 761-842.json, Concrete_1-50.json, Concrete_101-150.json, Concrete_151-200.json, Concrete_50-100.json, conc_201-250.json, conc_250-300.json, conc_301-350.json, conc_350-405.json

questions.q: 52. Sand requiring a high water cement ratio, belongs to
questions.explain: Zone I sand is the coarsest grading zone; coarse sand has less surface area, but due to its grading it requires a comparatively higher water-cement ratio to achieve workability.

questions.q: 96. Water cement ratio is
options: volume of water to that of cement
weight of water to that of cement
weight of concrete to that of water
volume of concrete to that of water
questions.explain: Water-cement ratio can be expressed either by volume of water to cement or by weight of water to cement, hence both (a) and (b) are correct.

questions.q: 97. Water cement ratio by weight is
options: higher as compared to that by volume
questions.explain: Since cement has a higher specific gravity than water, the water-cement ratio expressed by weight is numerically higher than that expressed by volume.

questions.q: 98. Water cement ratio is generally expressed in volume of water required per
questions.explain: Water-cement ratio is commonly expressed in terms of litres of water required per 50 kg (one bag) of cement.

questions.q: 99. Water cement ratio is normally used
questions.explain: For most practical concrete mixes, the normally used water-cement ratio ranges between 0.4 and 0.5 to achieve adequate strength and workability.

questions.q: 101. The maximum water required for w/c ratio is
questions.explain: Lower grade mixes are leaner and are permitted a higher water-cement ratio; among the grades listed, M10 (the leanest, lowest-strength mix) is allowed the maximum w/c ratio and hence the maximum water content.

questions.q: 102. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following
options: A rich mix of concrete possesses lesser strength than a lean mix of desired workability with excessive quantity of water
The strength of concrete decreases as the water cement ratio increases
If the water cement ratio is less than 0.45, the concrete is not workable and causes honey-combed structure
Good compaction by mechanical vibrations increases the strength of concrete
questions.explain: This is false: for a given workability, a rich mix needs less water and therefore has a lower w/c ratio, which gives it HIGHER strength than a lean mix that needs excess water to achieve the same workability.

questions.q: 103. According to Water-Cement ratio Law, the strength of workable plastic concrete
options: Depends upon the amount of water used in the mix
Does not depend upon the quality of cement mixed with aggregates
Does not depend upon the quantity of cement mixed with aggregates
questions.explain: Abrams' Water-Cement Ratio Law states that, for fully workable plastic concrete, strength is governed only by the w/c ratio and is independent of the cement quantity or quality used, provided the mix is workable.

questions.q: 104. The minimum amount of water cement ratio for complete hydration of cement is
questions.explain: Complete chemical and physical hydration of cement requires approximately 0.40 water-cement ratio by weight (chemical combination alone needs about 0.25, but 0.40 accounts for gel water/physical absorption as well).

questions.q: 105. The condition not applicable to water cement ratio law, is
options: Internal moisture conditions on hydration continue till complete strength is gained
Concrete specimens may be tested at any temperature
Concrete specimens need be of same age
questions.explain: The Water-Cement Ratio Law assumes standard, controlled testing conditions; testing specimens 'at any temperature' violates the law's requirement of comparable curing/testing conditions, so this condition is NOT applicable.

questions.q: 107. C.R.R.I. charts are used to obtain a relationship between strength of concrete and
questions.explain: Central Road Research Institute (C.R.R.I.) charts plot compressive strength of concrete against the water-cement ratio, allowing quick estimation of the w/c ratio needed for a target strength.

questions.q: 130. The strength of concrete is directly proportional to
questions.explain: Strength varies inversely with the water-cement ratio, which is the same as saying it is directly proportional to the cement-water ratio (i.e., more cement relative to water gives higher strength).

questions.q: 146. The lower water cement ratio in concrete, introduces
options: Greater wear resistance and improved bond strength
questions.explain: A lower w/c ratio produces a denser, less porous cement paste, which simultaneously reduces creep/shrinkage, lowers permeability, improves frost resistance, and increases wear resistance and bond strength — all of the above.

questions.q: 164. When water cement ratio is increased; workability
questions.explain: Increasing the water cement ratio makes the mix more fluid and easier to work with, thus increasing workability (though it reduces strength).

questions.q: 166. Workability of concrete in which low water cement ratio is determined by
questions.explain: The compaction factor test is more suitable and sensitive for measuring workability of stiff/low workability (low w/c ratio) mixes where the slump test is not effective.

questions.q: 182. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the quality of water governs the strength of concrete
the quality of water required for concreting, depends upon the grading of aggregate and method of compaction
10% excess of water reduces the strength of concrete by 15%
30% excess of water reduces the strength of concrete by 50%
questions.explain: All these statements about the effect of water quality and excess water quantity on concrete strength are established facts in concrete technology, hence all are correct.

questions.q: 186. If P, Y and Z are the weights of cement, fine aggregates and coarse aggregates respectively and W/C is the water to be added to first batch, is obtained by the equation
questions.explain: This is the standard empirical formula (0.3p + 0.1y + 0.012z = W/C x p) used to estimate the water to be added to the first trial batch based on the absorption characteristics of the mix ingredients.

questions.q: 187. If 50 kg of fine aggregates and 100kg of coarse aggregates re mixed in a concrete whose water cement ratio is 0.6, the weight of water required for harsh mix, is
questions.explain: Using the standard empirical relation for harsh mixes and given the fine and coarse aggregate quantities along with the specified w/c ratio of 0.6, the calculated water requirement works out to 12 kg.

questions.q: 190. Shrinkage in cement concrete can be reduced by using
questions.explain: All these measures - low w/c ratio, reduced cement content, properly proportioned mix, and use of pre-saturated aggregates - help in minimizing drying shrinkage of concrete.

questions.q: 217. The modulus of elasticity of concrete improves with
questions.explain: As concrete matures/ages, continued hydration increases its density and strength, which in turn improves (increases) its modulus of elasticity.

questions.q: 274. For batching 1:3:6 and water cement ratio 0.6 both by weight, the quantity of water required per bag, is
questions.explain: For a 50 kg cement bag with a water-cement ratio of 0.6 by weight, the water required = 0.6 x 50 = 30 kg.

questions.q: 284. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the diameter of the pipe line used for transportation of concrete by pumps does not exceed 30 cm
the slump of the concrete to be pumped should not be less that 5 cm and more
the water cement ratio of concrete to be pumped is kept between 0.5 to 0.65.
number of bends provided in the pipe line should be minimum
questions.explain: All these are correct standard requirements for pumpable concrete - restricted pipe diameter, minimum slump requirement, controlled w/c ratio, and minimizing pipe bends for efficient pumping.

questions.q: 368. If water cement ratio is more,
options: the durability of the concrete will be more
the durability of the concrete will be less
the durability of the concrete will not be affected
questions.explain: A higher water-cement ratio increases the porosity and permeability of hardened concrete, which reduces its durability against attack by external agents.

questions.q: 369. Low water-cement ratio in concrete:
options: improves the frost resistance of concrete
questions.explain: A low water-cement ratio produces a denser paste, which simultaneously lowers permeability, raises compressive strength, and improves resistance to frost/freeze-thaw damage.

questions.q: 379. Reduction in aggregate - cement ratio while keeping W/C ratio constant causes :
questions.explain: Reducing the aggregate-cement ratio means using more cement paste relative to aggregate, which, at the same water-cement ratio, provides more lubrication and thus increases workability.

questions.q: 385. The strength of concrete increase with decreases in :
questions.explain: Strength of concrete is inversely related to the water-cement ratio — as the water-cement ratio decreases, the paste becomes denser and strength increases (Abrams' law).

questions.q: 57. The rule of water cement ratio was established by
questions.explain: The water-cement ratio law, relating strength of concrete inversely to the water-cement ratio, was established by Duff Abrams in 1918.

questions.q: 58. Water-cement ratio is, usually, expressed in
options: liters of water required per bag of cement
liters of water required per kg of cement
questions.explain: Water-cement ratio can be conveniently expressed in either liters of water per bag of cement or liters of water per kg of cement, since both are equivalent ways of expressing the same ratio.

questions.q: 62. If 30 % excess water is added, the strength of concrete is reduced by
questions.explain: Excess water disproportionately weakens concrete strength; adding 30% excess water can reduce the resulting strength by as much as 50%, according to established water-cement ratio relationships.

questions.q: 86. The strength of concrete is directly proportional to
questions.explain: According to Abram's law, strength varies inversely with water-cement ratio, which is the same as saying strength is directly proportional to the cement-water ratio.

questions.q: 87. The strength of concrete increases with increase in
questions.explain: Concrete strength benefits from a lower water-cement ratio, appropriately larger aggregate (up to a limit for better interlocking), and finer cement particles that hydrate faster, so all these factors together increase strength.

questions.q: 113. The condition not applicable to water cement ratio law, is
options: internal moisture conditions on hydration continue till complete strength is gained
concrete specimens may be tested at any temperature
concrete specimens need be of same age
concrete specimens need be of same size
questions.explain: The water-cement ratio law assumes standard curing conditions; testing specimens 'at any temperature' is not a valid assumption of the law, since temperature affects hydration and thus strength results.

questions.q: 122. Workability of concrete mix with low water cement ratio is determined by
questions.explain: For low workability, stiff concrete mixes with low water-cement ratios, the compaction factor test gives more reliable and sensitive results than the slump test.

questions.q: 131. Shrinkage in concrete can be reduced by using
questions.explain: Shrinkage can be minimized through multiple combined measures: keeping water-cement ratio low, reducing cement content, and using pre-saturated (pre-wetted) aggregates, all reducing moisture loss and paste volume.

questions.q: 163. Strength of concrete increases with
questions.explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area and hydrate faster and more completely, contributing to increased strength of concrete.

questions.q: 187. Water cement ratio by weight is
options: Higher as compared to that by volume
Lower is compared to that by volume
questions.explain: Since cement is heavier than an equal volume of water, expressing the water-cement ratio by weight generally yields a higher numerical value compared to expressing it by volume.

questions.q: 189. Shrinkage in concrete can be reduced by
options: Using tight and non-absorbent from work
questions.explain: Shrinkage can be minimized through combined measures: reducing water-cement ratio, selecting suitable low-shrinkage aggregates, and using tight, non-absorbent formwork to retain moisture.

questions.q: 193. If water cement ratio is 0.7 by weight, then the quantity of water required in concrete while using one full bag will be
questions.explain: With a water-cement ratio of 0.7 and one bag of cement weighing 50kg, the water required is 0.7 × 50 = 35kg.

questions.q: 201. Minimum water cement ratio required for fully hydration of cement is
questions.explain: A water-cement ratio of about 0.38 is theoretically required for complete hydration of cement, ensuring all cement particles react fully with water.

questions.q: 218. Minimum required water cement ratio for a workable concrete, is
questions.explain: A minimum water-cement ratio of about 0.40 is generally required to produce a workable concrete mix that can be properly placed and compacted.

questions.q: 232. For constant w/c ratio if the aggregate/cement ratio is reduced, the workability of concrete
questions.explain: Reducing the aggregate-cement ratio (i.e., using relatively more cement paste) while keeping water-cement ratio constant provides more paste to lubricate the aggregates, increasing workability.

questions.q: 234. Sand requiring a high water cement ratio belongs to
questions.explain: Zone I sand consists of relatively coarser grading with higher surface irregularity, requiring a higher water-cement ratio to achieve the necessary workability.

questions.q: 240. The minimum water-cement ratio to obtain workable concrete is
questions.explain: A minimum water-cement ratio of about 0.40 is generally needed to produce a concrete mix with sufficient workability for proper placement and compaction.
